newsitem.title: USA: Clinton welcomes date for NATO enlargement summit.
newsitem.headline: Clinton welcomes date for NATO enlargement summit.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Tuesday welcomed NATO's decision to hold a July 1997 summit to invite new members to join the western security alliance.

Speaking at a White House event to mark International Human Rights Day, Clinton said the summit would "carry forward our goal of building a Europe that is undivided, democratic and at peace for the first time in history."

"One in which we will work to forge a partnership with Russia, adapt NATO to the demands of the new era, and invite the first aspiring members from among Europe's new democracies into NATO," he added. "My goal is to see them become full members of the alliance for NATO's 50th birthday in 1999."

Earlier, NATO officials meeting in Brussels said the leaders of the 16 member alliance would gather at a special July 8-9 summit in Madrid to invite new members to join the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).
The United States has not made public which countries it wants to join the alliance first, but Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are widely seen as the frontrunners.
Clinton in October first set 1999 as the target date to welcome new members into the alliance. REUTER
